findings.title: limitFunction drops all caller arguments
findings.cause: The returned wrapper changed from forwarding `...arguments_` into `function_` to a zero-argument wrapper: `return () => limit(() => function_());`.
findings.impact: Any reusable limited function that needs arguments now calls the original function with no arguments. The documented recipe `urls.map(url => limitedFetchUrl(url))` would call `fetchUrl(undefined)`, and TypeScript still advertises an argument-preserving wrapper.
evidence: Current source: index.js:121-124 returns a zero-argument wrapper.
Public contract: index.d.ts:133-136 returns `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`.
Public recipe: recipes.md:161-163 calls `limitedFetchUrl(url)`.
Historical diff: HEAD:index.js:120 forwarded `...arguments_`.
Mission verification: clm_2_1779060224773, direct evidence grade.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused in-memory Node probe with a Queue stub: `const limited = limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1}); await limited('sentinel')` returned `undefined` instead of `sentinel`.

findings.title: limit.map no longer passes indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: `limit.map` now computes `iterableIsArray` and passes `undefined` as the mapper index for Sets, iterators, and other non-array iterables.
findings.impact: The README and type comments say the mapper receives the item value and its index and is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))`. Consumers using Sets or generators with index-aware mappers silently receive `undefined`.
evidence: Current source: index.js:107-112 passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`.
Public contract: readme.md:78-84 says the mapper receives the item value and its index.
Type contract: index.d.ts:30-43 documents and types the second mapper parameter as `index: number`.
Existing tests cover Set/iterator values but not their indexes: test.js:239-254.
Mission verification: clm_3_1779060241935, direct evidence grade.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused in-memory Node probe: `await limit.map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (value, index) => value + ':' + index)` produced `["a:undefined","b:undefined"]` instead of `["a:0","b:1"]`.

findings.title: Options-object default makes clearQueue reject by default
findings.cause: The options destructuring changed the default from `rejectOnClear = false` to `rejectOnClear = true` when `pLimit` receives an object.
findings.impact: `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` no longer behaves like `pLimit(1)` for `clearQueue()`. Pending promises reject with `AbortError` by default even though README, recipes, and types say `rejectOnClear` defaults to false and discarded pending promises normally never settle.
evidence: Current source: index.js:6-8 defaults `rejectOnClear` to true for options objects.
Public contract: readme.md:46-52 says default false.
Type contract: index.d.ts:99-106 says default false.
Recipe contract: recipes.md:76-78 says promises for discarded tasks never settle.
Historical diff: HEAD:index.js:7 defaulted `rejectOnClear` to false.
Mission verification: clm_5_1779060241995, direct evidence grade.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused in-memory Node probe queued one running and one pending task with `pLimit({concurrency: 1})`, called `clearQueue()`, and observed `rejected:AbortError`; expected default behavior was `still-pending`.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass runtime validation
findings.cause: Runtime validation changed from `typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean'` to `rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean'`, so falsy non-booleans skip the TypeError path.
findings.impact: JavaScript consumers can pass invalid values such as `0`, `''`, or `null` and get accepted silently, contradicting the boolean-only API and weakening runtime contract checks.
evidence: Current source: index.js:12 validates only truthy non-boolean values.
Historical source: HEAD:index.js:12 rejected every non-boolean value.
Type contract: index.d.ts:99-106 declares `rejectOnClear?: boolean`.
Type-only test exists for a truthy string, but no runtime test covers falsy non-booleans: index.test-d.ts:29.
Mission verification: clm_6_1779060242027, direct evidence grade.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused in-memory Node probe: `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})` was accepted; expected `TypeError`.

findings.title: Infinity concurrency is rejected despite prior supported no-limit behavior
findings.cause: `validateConcurrency` now requires `Number.isInteger(concurrency)` and removed the explicit `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` allowance.
findings.impact: Callers using `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` as an unlimited-concurrency configuration now get a synchronous TypeError. This is a behavioral regression from the previous implementation and from the common interpretation of a numeric minimum-only concurrency limit.
evidence: Current source: index.js:127-130 rejects non-integers, including Infinity.
Historical source: HEAD:index.js:123-125 explicitly accepted `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`.
README/API: readme.md:37-44 describes a numeric concurrency limit with minimum 1 and does not document removal of Infinity.
No existing test covers Infinity in test.js:275-303.
Mission verification: clm_4_1779060241963, direct evidence grade.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused in-memory Node probe: `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)` threw `TypeError: Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up`.
